cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand-drawn batik cotton sarong with a north-coast Javanese style kepala/badan design, described as such in the museum record; batik sarongs like this are worn across Java and Bali and are plausible Balinese dress, matching the claimed garment category.

physical.title: skirt; sarong
physical.summary: A cotton (tabby) batik tube skirt, a 'sarung', hand-drawn, mostly one-sided?  Probably from north coast, in strong colours, crudely finished.  'Kepala' has blue background, scalloped sides separated from blue inner border only by a very narrow scalloped strip achieved, as with most of the design in the 'kepala' and within border, in very dark red, probably produced by overpainting the blue.  Design in 'kepala' originally outlined in narrow line of wax, some parts which remain white filled in with wax, mainly some of the large petals of the main flower design in the 'kepala', some scattered small flowers and part of the wings of a butterfly.  The 'kepala' is only 8 cms away from the right hand edge of the cloth. Top border, which has a straight edge, is in dark brown with blue and white detailing.  'Badan' is of diagonal bands, the widest with a striped background, just off vertical, against which are set highly stylised shapes which may be animal or floral.  Another set of bands are gringsing (scales) with leaf shapes set against them. Between these two types are narrower bands in threes, blue triangles on the outer and dark stripes on the inner.  Narrow sisir stripes along long edges.   [Text written by Dr Fiona Kerlogue, Horniman Museum.]
